_meta.source: Prism/BookIII.md — the compound catalog (Common, Alloy, Biological, Mineral, Useful, Gemstone Compounds). Transcribed faithfully; the engine's compound catalog was previously deferred (BookIII: 'the exact mapping from these tables to classified materials is unassigned — the world simulation works element->material directly'). This file lands it.
_meta.split: Ids 1-78 = gameplay compound catalog (Prism BookIII transcription, the source prototype for the materials map). Ids 79-96 = the mantle + world-formation-simulation compounds, moved to the sibling crust_compounds.json on 2026-08-19 to keep the gameplay and world-sim material-slot budgets legible. ONE shared id space across both files - ids are globally unique and never reused (see retired_ids). flicker-materials (src/source.rs::load_compounds) loads BOTH files into a single in-memory catalog, so every consumer resolves any compound by name/id regardless of which file it lives in.
_meta.schema: Each row: id, name, formula (ASCII, verbatim from the book — may reference elements outside the Prism 28-element table (ceiling 30; count per periodic_table.json _meta.additions)), category (common|mineral|useful|gemstone|biological|alloy), elements[{symbol,count}] (PARSED constituents, restricted to Prism periodic_table.json elements — non-Prism symbols like F in Apatite's formula are dropped from this list but kept in `formula`), natural (true = forms in-world during world-gen; false = a crafted alloy/recipe), hardness_mohs / density_g_cm3 / brittleness (0..1) — ONE TABLE (Aaron, 2026-07-13): populated on EVERY row, no split populations. Real-world reference values; for the 78 Book III rows they are proposed-starting-values pending ratification (the R6b twelve were ruled with theirs); 0.0 hardness/brittleness = not applicable (non-solid), the element-table gas convention. Quench/cooling-rate is deliberately NOT a column here: per R4b it is per-layer formation provenance, combined with these constants by the R7 conditions registry. extracted_element (ore target, omitted if none), harvestable (true = curated mineable ore/gem that must reach a concentrated vein; curated gameplay canon — NOT extended by the R6b merge; spodumene/dolomite ore notes await a separate ruling), sim_required (true = row added beyond the Book III transcription for the world-sim — the R6b minerals 79-90 and the gas species 91-96, now in crust_compounds.json, plus the biological Lignin/Cellulose/Oils that remain here), uses (Book rows) / note (R6b rows) — sparse text fields.
_meta.use: Loaded by flicker-materials Tables via TableSource (JsonTableSource reads this as a sibling of periodic_table.json/materials.json). The composition->compound classifier + the mineral extraction wiring to the node/vein layer are the next step. Since 2026-08-19 the mantle/world-formation-sim compounds (ids 79-96) live in the sibling crust_compounds.json, appended into this same catalog at load (see _meta.split).

retired_ids.42: Feldspar — the Books' combined two-formula row (KAlSi3O8, NaAlSi3O8), superseded by the R6b split rows Albite (82) and Orthoclase (83); ruled retired by Aaron 2026-07-13. Ids are stable — NEVER reuse a retired id. (Albite/Orthoclase now live in crust_compounds.json.)

_meta.crystallizes: crystallizes (minerals only) = this phase forms by CRYSTALLISATION from a melt or from solution circulating in rock, so the Crystallization stage may make it. FALSE for phases with a different route: Halite/Sylvite/Saltpeter are evaporites (need standing water to dry out), Coal is made from buried tissue by Maturation, Bauxite is a tropical weathering residue. Replaces the stage's former filter on sim_required, which is a PROVENANCE flag (which book a row came from) and was never a statement about what can form - using it as one is why ore was a bare number and never a mineral, and why quartz, and therefore sandstone/chert/quartzite, could not exist (2026-08-06).
_meta.metamorphic: metamorphic = {to, pressure_pa, temp_k}: the PHYSICAL stability limit of the phase - under at least this peak pressure and peak temperature (Layer.peak_pt, the worst a bed has ever endured) it reorganises into 'to'. These are the real numbers for the reaction and are NOT chosen against what any particular world can reach: a threshold no ground attains simply means that world never made the phase, which is a fact about the world and not an error to correct (DO NOT ENCODE RULES FOR OUTCOMES). The reaction must be ELEMENT-NEUTRAL - both phases the same elements in the same proportions - checked at load; anything releasing a volatile needs a reaction that books it too, and is not expressible here yet.

compounds.name: Water
compounds.uses: Essential for plant growth and biological functions, drives erosion and sediment transport, and is used in crafting and alchemical recipes.

compounds.name: Carbon Dioxide
compounds.uses: Vital for plant photosynthesis, influences environmental and atmospheric dynamics, and features in crafting and chemical reactions.

compounds.name: Silicon Dioxide
compounds.uses: A fundamental material for crafting glass and ceramics, used in building structures and advanced items, and integral to making molds and casting components.

compounds.name: Calcium Carbonate
compounds.uses: Essential for construction materials like cement and mortar, used in decorative items and sculptures, and influences soil pH affecting plant growth.

compounds.name: Iron Oxide
compounds.uses: Used for coloring materials and crafting pigments, important for tools, weapons and building materials, and can indicate iron deposits for mining.

compounds.name: Sodium Chloride
compounds.uses: Used in food preservation and seasoning, essential in chemical processes and crafting recipes, and employed in curing hides and preserving materials.

compounds.name: Potassium Nitrate
compounds.uses: A key fertilizer ingredient for plant growth, used in crafting gunpowder for explosives, and involved in food preservation techniques.

compounds.name: Copper Sulfate
compounds.uses: Employed in crafting fungicides and pesticides, used in chemical processes and as a mordant in dyeing, and part of advanced crafting and alchemy recipes.

compounds.name: Phosphoric Acid
compounds.uses: Essential in producing fertilizers, used in various industrial and crafting processes, and involved in rust removal and metal treatment.

compounds.name: Halite
compounds.uses: Common salt used for food preservation, seasoning, glass and hide tanning, and as a chlorine source for disinfectants.

compounds.name: Sylvite
compounds.uses: Key fertilizer ingredient for plant growth and a component in chemical and alchemical recipes.

compounds.name: Calcite
compounds.uses: Primary construction material (cement, mortar, concrete) also used to adjust soil pH and for building with limestone and marble.

compounds.name: Ilmenite
compounds.uses: Source of titanium for advanced tools, armor, high-strength alloys, and specialized machinery.

compounds.name: Chromite
compounds.uses: Used to craft stainless steel and corrosion-resistant materials, boosting tool durability and metal finishes.

compounds.name: Hematite
compounds.uses: Abundant early-game iron source for tools, weapons, building materials, and steel when combined with carbon.

compounds.name: Linnaeite
compounds.uses: Cobalt source for magnets, advanced alloys, and high-tech equipment that adds strength and durability.

compounds.name: Millerite
compounds.uses: Nickel source for stainless steel, coinage, specialty alloys, and corrosion resistance.

compounds.name: Chalcopyrite
compounds.uses: Copper source for electrical components, wiring, tools, construction, and bronze when alloyed with tin.

compounds.name: Sphalerite
compounds.uses: Zinc source for galvanization against rust, brass with copper, and other alloys and metal treatments.

compounds.name: Argentite
compounds.uses: Silver source valued for currency, jewelry, ceremonial objects, and highly conductive electrical components.

compounds.name: Native Platinum
compounds.uses: Extremely rare and valuable platinum for advanced technology, high-end crafting, and catalytic processes.

compounds.name: Native Gold
compounds.uses: Gold for currency, jewelry, prestigious items, trade, wealth, and high-end electronics.

compounds.name: Uraninite
compounds.uses: Rare uranium source for advanced technology, energy, high-level quests, and powerful unique artifacts.

compounds.name: Bauxite
compounds.uses: Lightweight aluminum for crafting, construction, utensils, alloys, transportation devices, and structures.

compounds.name: Coal
compounds.uses: Fuel source for smelting and heating, processable into graphite, and essential to steel production with iron.

compounds.name: Quartz
compounds.uses: Silicon source for glass, ceramics, silicon components, molds, and high-temperature materials.

compounds.name: Cassiterite
compounds.uses: Tin source for bronze with copper, pewter, solder, and coating or plating processes.

compounds.name: Galena
compounds.uses: Lead source for batteries, pipes, radiation shielding, weights, ammunition, and protective equipment.

compounds.name: Saltpeter
compounds.uses: Nitrogen source essential for fertilizers, gunpowder, and food preservation.

compounds.name: Apatite
compounds.uses: Phosphorus source vital for fertilizers, soil fertility, and certain alloys and chemical compounds.

compounds.name: Native Sulfur
compounds.uses: Elemental sulfur for gunpowder, matches, insecticides, vulcanizing rubber, alchemy, and chemical processes.

compounds.name: Flint
compounds.uses: Microcrystalline quartz used to make sharp tools, weapons, and fire-starting sparks for survival and hunting.

compounds.name: Gypsum
compounds.uses: Calcium sulfate dihydrate used in construction plaster, soil conditioning for agriculture, and crafting molds and casts.

compounds.name: Slate
compounds.uses: Fine-grained metamorphic rock used as a building material for roofing and flooring and for writing tablets and blackboards.

compounds.name: Limestone
compounds.uses: Calcium carbonate used in building construction, road-making, producing lime for mortar and cement, and decorative sculpting.

compounds.name: Sandstone
compounds.uses: Sand-particle rock used in construction for buildings and paving and carved into statues and architectural details.

compounds.name: Obsidian
compounds.uses: Silica-rich volcanic glass used to craft sharp blades and arrowheads and valued for decorative cutting tools.

compounds.name: Granite
compounds.uses: Durable coarse-grained igneous rock used extensively in construction, monuments, sculptures, and large-scale building projects.

compounds.name: Clay
compounds.uses: Hydrated aluminum silicate essential for pottery, bricks, ceramics, tiles, and early settlement development.

compounds.name: Charcoal
compounds.uses: Carbon-rich material used as fuel and in smelting metals, blacksmithing, and gunpowder production.

compounds.name: Graphite
compounds.uses: Pure carbon used in pencils, lubricants, refractory materials, electrodes, and battery components, and can be processed into diamonds.

compounds.name: Diamond
compounds.uses: Crafts high-durability tools and weapons and serves as a rare, high-value jewelry and trade item that encourages deep mining.

compounds.name: Emerald
compounds.uses: Crafted into jewelry and ornamental items, valued for its vibrant green color, and usable in quests or magical artifacts.

compounds.name: Ruby
compounds.uses: Valued for its deep red color in jewelry and used to craft decorative and ceremonial items with possible magical properties.

compounds.name: Sapphire
compounds.uses: Used in jewelry and high-end crafting, available in various colors depending on impurities, and may link to quests or special abilities.

compounds.name: Amethyst
compounds.uses: Used in decorative items and jewelry, found in geodes or special rock formations, and valued for its aesthetic appeal.

compounds.name: Topaz
compounds.uses: Used in crafting and as a trade commodity, valued for its range of colors and clarity.

compounds.name: Opal
compounds.uses: Known for its iridescent play-of-color, used in unique jewelry pieces, and may grant luck or special in-game effects.

compounds.name: Garnet
compounds.uses: Used in crafting and as an abrasive material, valued for its deep red color in jewelry.

compounds.name: Pearl
compounds.uses: Crafted into jewelry and decorative items, harvested from oysters or found in treasure chests, symbolizing wealth and rarity.

compounds.name: Turquoise
compounds.uses: Valued for its blue-green color in jewelry, used to craft talismans or amulets, and associated with protection and healing.

compounds.name: Lignin
compounds.uses: Provides rigidity and decay resistance in plants and can be processed into crafting/construction materials affecting wooden-structure durability.

compounds.name: Cellulose
compounds.uses: Gives plants structural support and can be made into paper, textiles, ropes, and fabrics.

compounds.name: Chlorophyll
compounds.uses: Essential for photosynthesis and usable in crafting dyes, pigments, and alchemical effects.

compounds.name: Resin
compounds.uses: Used to craft adhesives, varnishes, sealants, torches, and flammable or medicinal/alchemical materials.

compounds.name: Nectar
compounds.uses: Attracts pollinators and can be collected to make sweeteners, fermented beverages, or alchemical potions.

compounds.name: Pollen
compounds.uses: Affects character allergies, drives plant breeding and agriculture, and serves as a crafting or alchemy reagent.

compounds.name: Humus
compounds.uses: Enhances soil fertility and plant growth, boosting crop yields and player farming.

compounds.name: Wax
compounds.uses: Used to craft candles, polishes, waterproofing, and metal-casting molds, plus healing salves and protective coatings.

compounds.name: Oils
compounds.uses: Used for cooking, crafting, and lamp fuel, and in soaps, lotions, medicines, and alchemy recipes.

compounds.name: Brass
compounds.uses: Crafted into musical instruments, decorative fittings, and jewelry, valued for acoustics, corrosion resistance, and easy machinability.

compounds.name: Pewter
compounds.uses: Cast into tableware, tankards, figurines, and ornaments as an affordable silver-like alternative with a low melting point.

compounds.name: Cast Iron
compounds.uses: Used for cookware, pipes, machinery parts, and heavy infrastructure requiring good heat retention and compressive strength.

compounds.name: Solder
compounds.uses: Joins and repairs metal parts in tinwork, plumbing, jewelry, and electrical circuitry via its low melting point.

compounds.name: Sterling Silver
compounds.uses: Crafted into durable jewelry, utensils, coinage, and antimicrobial medical instruments, with copper strengthening the soft silver.

compounds.name: Electrum
compounds.uses: Used for historical coinage, jewelry, and ceremonial objects as a symbol of wealth and status.

compounds.name: Gunmetal
compounds.uses: Cast into cannons, guns, machinery, and marine fittings for strength and saltwater corrosion resistance.

compounds.name: Nickel Silver
compounds.uses: Made into cutlery, instruments, jewelry, and outdoor fixtures with a silvery, corrosion-resistant finish despite containing no silver.

compounds.name: Wrought Iron
compounds.uses: Forged into gates, railings, decorative ironwork, tools, and historical structures for its ductility and toughness.

compounds.name: White Gold
compounds.uses: Used for jewelry, ornamental pieces, and gemstone settings, whitened and hardened by nickel.

compounds.name: Phosphor Bronze
compounds.uses: Used for springs, bolts, bearings, and musical instrument strings for its wear resistance and stiffness.

compounds.name: Aluminum Bronze
compounds.uses: Used for marine hardware, pumps, coins, and medals for its seawater corrosion resistance and golden appearance.

compounds.name: Carbon Steel
compounds.uses: Used for construction materials, tools, and blades where higher carbon content increases hardness and strength.

compounds.name: Stainless Steel
compounds.uses: Used for corrosion-resistant tools, cookware, and hygienic medical instruments thanks to its protective chromium oxide layer.

compounds.name: Bell Metal
compounds.uses: Cast into resonant bells, gongs, sculptures, and occasional coinage, using a higher tin content than bronze.

compounds.name: Billon
compounds.uses: Used to mint lower-value coins and make economical jewelry with a high copper proportion.

compounds.name: Cupro-Nickel
compounds.uses: Used for modern coinage, medals, and seawater-exposed marine engineering for its wear and corrosion resistance.
